turns.question: So does that mean cobras and elephants were in the same place at the same time?
turns.answer:
No. It only means some Indian cobra records were within 10 km of some elephant records inside the 75 km search area around EBTL.

Local:
This was not an exact EBTL property check. It used an approximate 75 km area around EBTL.

Regional:
The match is in the wider area around EBTL, not proof of the same exact spot.

Observed:
No direct observation here shows a cobra and an elephant together at the same time.

Reported:
The result used reported occurrence records for cobra and elephant.

Proxy:
This is a proximity result from record locations. It does not show same-time presence, interaction, or shared use of one site.

Modelled:
None.

For each sighting or sign, record GPS point, date, time, species, and photo if possible, and note if both species were observed on the same visit.

turns.question: What information do we need to know that properly?
turns.answer:
To know that properly, we need direct same-visit evidence, not just nearby records.

Local:
We need exact EBTL property boundaries and exact on-site locations, because the earlier check used an approximate 75 km area around EBTL.

Regional:
We need to know which records are actually from the EBTL area versus elsewhere in the wider 75 km search area.

Observed:
We need direct field observations showing cobra and elephant at the same place and time, or very close in time on the same site visit.

Reported:
For each record, we need the exact date, exact time, exact GPS point, species identification, and record source.

Proxy:
The current result is only a proximity check between reported occurrence points. To interpret it better, we need matched record dates and times so we can tell whether nearby records were also close in time.

Modelled:
None.

What the field team can collect:
GPS location, date, time, species seen or signs found, photo if possible, observer name, and repeated surveys on the EBTL property. Camera traps or the same-day transect records for both species would help most.
